title: feat: support CWS projects and memory agreements
head: 01dc55b7c2d1dd4365f1bbaf3a21211d9a21566a
body:
Hieronymus can recognize CWS authoring and translation projects without installing CWS. A read-only project-context command exposes structural metadata without starting a daemon; bundled skills interpret the user’s free-text memory agreement independently of technical binding and internal authority.

Adds schema 1/2 discovery, safe direction/edition selection and direction-scoped public reads, sessions and rule applicability. Explicit project languages override legacy defaults. Skills preserve provenance, selected-transfer outcomes and review requirements when dependencies change. Includes current public-API fixtures for real-model qualification; no new runtime dependency or release/version bump.

Validation: 1,538 Rust tests passed (17 ignored), plus 21 final inspection/direction tests and explicit real ONNX qualification. Formatting, all-feature Clippy/rustdoc, 100 Bun script tests, 85 frontend tests, typecheck and build passed; affected resource/test checks passed after final edits. Both branches passed independent task and final reviews.

Coordinated native acceptance covers 32 bounded final host/scenario outcomes. Native direction runs demonstrate bounded ambiguity, while selected-direction isolation is established by deterministic tests. Claude H-only usable retrieval and interpretation of returned AI material remain unqualified; native protected CWS translation acceptance is not claimed.

Companion: https://github.com/InkyQuill/creative-writing-skills/pull/9. Each repository remains independently installable and testable. [Coordinated acceptance record](https://github.com/InkyQuill/creative-writing-skills/blob/d6689a521184c86a92f1328982cf5a55518967c6/docs/hieronymus-integration-acceptance.md).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added read-only CWS project inspection through the `project-context` command, with human-readable and JSON reports.
  - Added project and direction discovery, validation, and status diagnostics.
  - Added optional story-scope filtering across memory, recall, search, termbase, and session workflows.
  - Added language and direction context support for translation-aware searches.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Context and scope validation errors are now reported instead of being silently ignored.
  - Improved session selection to require matching story scopes.

- **Documentation**
  - Added guidance for project inspection, permissions, evidence, memory handling, and protected project content.

_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Use per-term decision identity, revision, and language values.**

`fixture.terms` is a `Vec<TermSpec>`, and the caller processes every term. A second term reuses the existing decision ID and causes `IdempotencyConflict`. After that ID is made unique, `expected_revision: 1` still causes `RevisionConflict` for another term in the same series. A term in a `ja` series also fails because the helper sends `en` as its source language. Pass the matching language pair, generate a unique decision ID per term, and track the current revision per series. The current fixture has one `en`→`ru` term, so it hides this maintenance defect.
